profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a publicly traded technology company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, WA. Its own website, focused on Power Automate, describes the product as a tool for automating workflows and business processes across apps, systems, and websites using AI-powered, digital, and robotic process automation. The site quotes a customer stating that a data validation process formerly requiring over 100 people can now be managed by just a few people using generative AI and Power Automate, and references a Gartner Magic Quadrant for Robotic Process Automation report dated 23 June 2025.

Microsoft tracks a broad portfolio of AI products spanning several categories. These include Microsoft Copilot embedded across Microsoft 365, Azure OpenAI Service for accessing OpenAI models within Azure with enterprise content filtering and data residency controls, Azure Machine Learning as an MLOps platform with AutoML and a model registry, and Power Automate AI for enterprise workflow automation with Copilot and data loss prevention integration. Developer-facing offerings include AutoGen, a multi-agent conversation framework from Microsoft Research, Semantic Kernel as a model-agnostic orchestration SDK for .NET, Python, and Java, and Microsoft Agent Framework, described as the successor to both Semantic Kernel and AutoGen with native MCP and A2A support planned for 2026. Additional products include Microsoft Designer for image and design generation, Microsoft Teams AI for meeting recaps and intelligent recap, SharePoint AI for enterprise content management, and Microsoft Clipchamp AI for video editing with auto-caption and text-to-speech features.

Microsoft reported revenue of $331,839,000,000 for the period ending 30 June 2026, filed as a 10-K with CIK 0000789019 and trading under the ticker MSFT. The held facts list two federal cases in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York in which Microsoft is a named party: The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, and Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc.
